newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Slim majority back Cardoso's re-election in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Slim majority back Cardoso's re-election in Brazil.

text.p: Nearly two-thirds of Brazilians favour rewriting the Constitution to allow re-election, but only 51 percent say President Fernando Henrique Cardoso should have a chance at a second term, a poll published on Sunday said.

The poll comes as the government prepares to set up next week a special committee in the Chamber of Deputies to debate re-election. Brazil's constitution currently limits presidents, state governors and mayors to one term, but Cardoso says he would seek to stand again in 1998 if the rule were revised.
Sixty-four percent of respondents in the poll said they backed the concept of re-election for presidents, 31 percent were against and five percent had no opinion, newspaper Jornal do Brasil reported.
But only 51 percent said Cardoso should benefit from any change to the Constitution, 44 percent said re-election should be reserved for future presidents and five percent had no opinion.
The poll by private market researchers Vox Populi interviewed 1,470 voters in Brazil's three biggest cities -- Sao Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Belo Horizonte. The margin of error was five percent.
